To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the overall efficiency of biomass production in microalgae is not only dependent on photosynthesis, but also on the energy balance from photon to biomass and on the energy input for the downstream processing of biomass into biofuel.

(1) high biomass productivity is always associated with high metabolic costs and (2) the energy input to convert algal biomass into biofuels and biorefinery products is higher than the energy content of the products.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new photobioreactor concepts which are adapted to the metabolic and kinetic limitations of the algal cell.
the development of a sustainable biorefinery process based on the use of microalgae as CO2 sequestering organisms.
the development of a sustainable and efficient algal biorefinery which can contribute to the energy supply of the future.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the energy balance is a useful tool to evaluate the different strategies for algal biotechnology.
the algal biotechnology must be developed as a part of a comprehensive strategy to improve the efficiency of the whole energy chain.
the algal bioenergy concept should be seen as a part of the future energy system, but not as a stand-alone energy source.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is not the photon to biomass efficiency which is the limiting factor, but it is the energy balance of the overall process.
algal biorefineries must be designed as a closed loop system, which includes CO2 sequestrations, biomass production, and biorefinement.
the algal cell is not the bottleneck in the production chain, but rather a bioreactor design which allows a maximum productivity with a minimum metabolic costs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the energy balance from photon to harvest-able biomass must be considered as a key tool to identify the limiting steps on the cellular level and to develop strategies for the improvement in algal biotechnology.
the energy balance from photon to harvest is a powerful tool to evaluate different strategies for improving the efficiency of algal biomass production.
the efficiency of algal biomass production is not limited to the photon conversion efficiency of the photosynthetic apparatus but also by the energy demand of the cellular metabolism.
